  "winner": "B",

    "Time to first paying customer: B can launch as a narrow Stripe-to-bank reconciliation tool with no mandatory licensing. A's own brief lists the timeline for these as an open question, so it is a gating risk inside a 90-day window.",
    "Feasibility of the core claim: A's differentiator, filing correctly in the country of residence too, is flagged by its own most sophisticated competitor as the unsolved 'hard part.' B's core task is described as mechanical and rules-based, which suits AI agents.",
    "Acquisition: B lists a free, targeted channel (Stripe App Marketplace, sourced) plus $0 organic channels where the pain is already discussed. A's only channel is paid Meta lead-gen, where its own brief says cost per lead is above a $27.66 blended average in a high-CPC vertical.",
    "Liability surface: A's mistakes mean incorrect tax filings for a sophisticated, vocal user base. B's SOC2 burden is described as commercially expected, not legally required to launch. That is a lighter barrier for winning one early customer.",
    "Demand evidence is comparable: both cite three sourced Reddit or Indie Hackers quotes and both anchor prices to live competitors. Demand does not separate them, so execution and regulatory risk decide it."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's case for rests on the claim that Atamatax, a solo-built tool, 'attract[s] customers' at $199-$799. The brief cites only Atamatax's own homepage for pricing and gives no evidence of customer count, revenue, or traction. The claim that a one-person build is validated is therefore unsupported. A's acquisition evidence is also weak: a generic cross-industry Meta CPL benchmark with no niche-specific data.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. B is clearly saturated: six or more direct competitors, several with free tiers that may cover solo-founder volumes, and no differentiating wedge stated. B's '$400-600/mo bookkeeper time' figure attributed to Growthy has no URL and its privacy-compliance specifics are marked [unsourced], so both count as missing. B wins mainly because A's regulatory gating and unsolved multi-jurisdiction scope make a paid customer within 90 days less plausible, not because B's demand or willingness-to-pay evidence is stronger."
